The wave

A coordinator turns one large task into three isolated lanes. Drive the replay to see tasks, sessions, worktrees, messages, a blocker, a sibling reply, and one report move through the same graph.

Beat 01 · intake

Take the task

The coordinator session works on one parent task. Its task is trusted launch control; later message bodies remain untrusted coordination material.

coordinator — commandCLI
tm8 session spawn --teammate tm…mara --task task…launch --workdir worktree --mode coordinator
returned shape · selected fieldsJSON

A session is the running terminal. working_on records active work on the task.

reached state future lane durable message IVrounded square = teammate author

Text alternative: a coordinator works on a parent task, creates three child tasks, spawns three worker sessions in separate worktrees, posts assignments on each child task, receives progress messages, sees the UI task become blocked, observes its worker message the API worker session, receives a threaded reply, then consolidates all child results into one message on the parent task.

01Why the wave stays legible

Tasks hold scope

The parent owns the outcome. Homogeneous child tasks carry the API, UI, and verification slices.

Sessions do work

Each running session has a working_on edge to its child task and an in_worktree edge to an isolated checkout.

Messages keep causality

Assignments, progress, blockers, and the final result remain durable messages on the entities where they matter.

One report fans in

The coordinator reads the three task threads, reconciles the results, then sends one summary to the parent task.

02What the replay means

Control and material stay distinct

The task passed at spawn is part of trusted launch control. A message body is untrusted data: durable material to inspect, not authority to rewrite the agent’s rules.

That boundary survives even when a message is delivered to a live session as its next turn.

Identity is structural

Every message carries its author as a member or teammate. The body does not get to claim who wrote it.

MVMara Vossmemberauthor.kind: member
IVIvyteammateauthor.kind: team_member
Honesty note coordinator and coordinated-worker shape behavior through the launch prompt. They are not server-enforced permission boundaries. Worktree isolation is separate: --workdir worktree provisions one isolated checkout per session.

03The verbs under the motion

The replay uses the public CLI surface. There is no special progress or report command: both are messages.

structure
tm8 entity create task "…" --parent <task-id>
tm8 session spawn --teammate <id> --task <task-id> --workdir worktree --mode coordinated-worker
tm8 task transition <task-id> blocked
communication
tm8 message send --to <task-id> "progress…"
tm8 message send --to <session-id> "question…"
tm8 message reply <message-id> "answer…"

A reply derives its task/session route and parent from the delivered message id. A running session is an address like any other entity; delivery becomes its next turn.
